recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any future refinement of the phrase mathematically equivalent in light of FHIR-39134 measurement-point examples should be handled as a separate wording review, not as a missing application of FHIR-31809.
issue_request: FHIR-31809 was a Published FHIR-core MedicinalProductIngredient change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking how a product/substance can remain the same when repeated strength values appear to differ across countries. The resolution and comments called for explaining that repetitions are representations of the same strength, not different strengths.
initial_application: The issue was applied in source history by 7f8ca2e76b, which updated Ingredient.substance.strength to say repeated strengths are mathematically equivalent representations of a single strength, and 464b98e6e7 carried that wording forward with neighboring Ingredient clarifications.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini marks Ingredient active and maps the old MedicinalProductIngredient artifact to Ingredient. Later Published issue FHIR-39134 revisited the same strength area and added examples for presentation, concentration, reference strength, and repeated measured strengths rather than reversing the FHIR-31809 wording. BRR minutes reference the FHIR-31809 reconciliation discussion, and targeted Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative StructureDefinition still states that Ingredient.substance.strength repetitions are mathematically equivalent representations of a single strength, and the registered examples provide adjacent context for related strength representations.
